findings.evidence: Pairing.lean's diff adds `namespace differentialSections` declarations defined via `normalize E _ ...` and `ext_of_eventually_nhdsNE`, and proved with `toChartGerm_eq_mk`, `OneForm.coeff_smul` and `MeromorphicFunction.coe_toChartGerm`. None of them mentions `residuePairing` or `Residue.*`. `Differential/Twist.lean` imports neither `Germ` nor `Residue.*`, so importing it from `Germ.lean` or a new sibling file creates no cycle.
findings.fix: Move the `differentialSections` part of the `MeromorphicMul` section next to `differentialSections.normalize` in `Differential/Twist.lean`, or into a new `Differential/MeromorphicMul.lean` that imports `Twist`, `Germ` and `FunctionField.Germ`. Keep only `PrincipalParts.residuePairing_meromorphicMul` in `Residue/Pairing.lean`. Pairing.lean's own `public import ...Differential.Twist` is needed only for these declarations (via `normalize`), so it moves with them.
findings.issue: `differentialSections.meromorphicAt_finitePart_smul_toOneForm`, `neg_le_order_finitePart_smul_toOneForm`, `meromorphicMul`, `toOneForm_meromorphicMul_eventuallyEq` and `toChartGerm_meromorphicMul` are general operations on global sections of `Ω_D`. They use only `normalize`/`ext_of_eventually_nhdsNE` (from `Twist`/`Sheaf`) and `toChartGerm` (from `Germ`), and nothing from residues. Putting them in the residue-pairing file hides reusable `Ω_D` API behind the residue imports.

summary: Multiplication of `Ω_D` global sections by a meromorphic function (`differentialSections.meromorphicMul` and its supporting lemmas) is placed in `Differential/Residue/Pairing.lean`, but it has nothing to do with residues and belongs with the `Ω_D` normalization/germ API. All other new declarations and imports are placed appropriately.
